_: Shared configuration. Neutral defaults live here and are committed; machine- and person-specific values go to config.local.json, which is git-ignored and merged on top.

mirror.rule: a task with a date or period but no time block becomes an all-day event with availability=FREE; backlog items and Noos's own technical tasks stay out of the calendar

codereview._: Nightly self code-review after the 05:00 restart (status/code-review-headless.sh, noos-codereview.timer). Fable 5, ultracode multi-agent; fixes High/Medium findings locally with a task + spec + test each, writes a scan report then a fix report under status/state/code-review/ (git-ignored), never pushes.

inbox._: status/bots/inbox.py reads what the owner writes to the named bots and answers in their voice. Only his chat id is answered — the bots are public; everything else is logged to status/state/bots/dropped.jsonl. The answering call has no tools and no MCP, so a message in those chats cannot make anything happen.

bots._: message kind → env suffix. notify.sh --bot <kind> sends through TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<SUFFIX> (and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID_<SUFFIX> if set) from .env.telegram, falling back to the main bot when the token is missing. Several kinds may share one suffix: news and youtube both live in Bruno's channel, spoken in his voice. The suffix is the bot's own name (Zirka, Bruno), not the kind, so a token is easy to match to the bot it came from. These are one-way broadcast channels: nothing polls getUpdates for them, so a reply sent to one of them never reaches the session.

voices._: name → ElevenLabs voice id. The real roster is personal and lives in config.local.json; notify.sh --voice <name> resolves through it.

roles._: message kind → profile name from voice.profiles. Unset kinds use the default voice and model from .env.voice.

profiles._: profile name → {voice, model, stability, speed, style, tempo, tags}. Audio tags ([зітхає], [тихо]) are only performed by eleven_v3/v4 models; multilingual_v2 reads them aloud. `speed` is ignored by those same v3/v4 models (measured), so `tempo` speeds the audio up after synthesis instead — see docs/voice-emotion.md.

usage._: ElevenLabs is a flat subscription, so what matters is the monthly credit quota, not a per-message price. The quota and what is already spent are read from the provider's own API (the account is shared with other agents), with the local voice log kept as this machine's share. Tokens are plain counters.

deepgram._: Needs a key with the usage:read scope; without it the probe falls back to the local log.

versions._: Previous contents of the files whose loss would hurt, kept beside them on the same disk (t1080). Not everything that gets rewritten: a cursor or a cache rebuilds itself, and versioning status/state/youtube.json alone would be ten megabytes a day of copied cursors. `keep` is a safety belt, not a retention policy — thinning by age, encryption and a copy off this machine are their own version. persona.md, CLAUDE.md and the systemd units joined the list with the panel's editors (t1103): git covers the first two only once something is committed, and a unit file is in no repository at all. Tools: tools/versions.py list|diff|restore.

permissions_: What may happen without asking — the one machine-readable copy of it (tools/permissions.py, t1102). start.sh renders this into the system prompt, so a change binds once the session restarts; the panel shows the levels and offers no switch, because permissions, secrets and tokens are set from the terminal only (the owner's standing rule). Levels: free | ask | never; anything unrecognised reads as never. Three rules are hard and absent from this block on purpose — see tools/permissions.py HARD.

panel._: The admin panel (panel/server.py, noos-panel.service). 8090 belongs to the matrix-agora panel. There is no authentication, so `host` decides who can reach it: 127.0.0.1 (an SSH tunnel only), `tailscale` (the owner's own devices), or 0.0.0.0 (every device on the local network). The owner chose the last one on 2026-10-31 — he works from another machine on the same Wi-Fi — knowing the board is unauthenticated. See docs/features/ADMIN-PANEL.md.
panel.auth_: The panel's login (t1100, phase 11). One shared password, hashed with scrypt into .env.panel (mode 600, git-ignored) by panel/auth.py set — from a terminal, never over HTTP or Telegram. Sessions live in the process, so a restart logs out. `host` above stays 0.0.0.0 because the machine the owner works from is not on the tailnet; narrowing to `tailscale` is one word the day it is.
panel.scenarios_: Screen 3 (t1101): the prompts that belong to no channel. `cmd` and `dry` are resolved against the repository root, and a leading *.py gets the project interpreter, so nothing hardcodes a path. `detach: true` means the run is long enough to need systemd-run — the request must not wait for it.

panel.journal_scope_: What the Rules screen's journal pane may show. `systemd` (default) — systemd's own lines for the unit: Starting / Finished / Failed / exit code / CPU time. `full` — the unit's own stdout too, which for a headless unit is the content a model composed (the digest's calendar block, mail subjects, the nightly review's findings) and therefore waits for the panel to have authentication (t1094).
panel.rules_masked_: Keys whose VALUE never reaches the Rules screen. The panel listens on the whole local network with no authentication (host above), so birth data, the calendar id, the owner's name and the ElevenLabs voice ids are shown as «перевизначено, значення приховано» — the fact of an override is useful, the value is nobody's business. Prefix match on whole dotted segments.
panel.key_files_: The key files the Rules screen reports on: present or missing, permissions, and the NAMES of the variables inside. Never a value.

astro._: The daily mood: the chart is computed locally (status/astro.py, Swiss Ephemeris / Moshier). Birth data is personal and lives in config.local.json under astro.birth.
